task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about the Stitch Hour Exchange, exploring what happens when neighbors trade repair time instead of paying each other cash.

facts.text: An August 2026 session note records Stitch Hour Exchange member Leda Marron shortening trousers while another member repaired a bag strap at the next table.
The exchange has 28 registered members and meets twice a month in a rented community room.
A completed job credits the worker and debits the requester with the same agreed amount of time.
One hour of agreed work earns one hour of credit, regardless of the member's usual commercial wage.
Credits cannot be redeemed for cash and do not guarantee that a particular skilled member will accept a request.
New members begin at zero and may owe up to two hours while arranging work they can contribute.
A $3 attendance charge pays toward room hire and shared thread, rather than purchasing an hour of another member's labor.
Members supply unusual fabrics, replacement zips or other job-specific materials themselves.
The ledger records 46 credited service hours for April through June 2026, excluding Veylan's coordination time; no cash valuation was recorded.
Four requested jobs were declined because no available member had the relevant skill or equipment.
Coordinator Omi Veylan spends about three hours a week arranging requests and updating the ledger without receiving either cash or time credits for that work.
Veylan said, "The hours can balance on the page while the person matching them is still running out of time."
Marron formerly altered clothes commercially and says teaching a beginner is different from promising a shop's turnaround time.
Marron said, "I can offer the skill, but I still need the freedom to say that a job is beyond this table."
Members agree the expected time before a repair and discuss changes if the work proves more involved.
The exchange does not guarantee a manufacturer's finish or accept repairs to safety-critical equipment.
Some members earn credits by organizing materials or setting up the room rather than sewing.
The organizers have not measured how many purchases were avoided or how participants' household finances changed.
The group began after a one-day coat-mending event in 2024 and stores its supplies in two wheeled cabinets.
The current room booking ends in December, and a proposed permanent workspace has no funding commitment.

forbidden_additions: Credits are cash, every request can be filled or the $3 charge buys a repair hour
